summary: You send a prompt, stare at a blank screen, and then the whole answer drops at once. The AI apps you use every day avoid that by streaming the answer word by word, and you can build the same thing into your own agents. Why AI apps show their answers word by word, and how to build that into your own agents. A language model already generates its answer one token at a time, each token predicted from everything before it. Streaming just sends each token the moment it's generated instead of waiting for the whole response. The model isn't any faster, but time to first token (TTFT) drops, so the app feels much quicker. Under the hood, the connection between your app and the server stays open, and the server pushes each token through it as it's produced, usually over HTTP streaming or Server-Sent Events (SSE).
